title: "Specializing to one model and one GPU is worth 1.2x to 6.7x"
description: "Published results where model-specific kernels and whole-model megakernels beat general engines, including a report that vLLM and SGLang use at most half of H100 bandwidth at low latency."
date: 2026-09-05

categories: [research, kernels, runtime]

**Question.** Does writing an engine for one model on one GPU actually pay, or
is the gain already captured by general engines with good kernels?

Method: published sources only. Nothing measured locally.

| source | specialized to | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [MPK megakernel](https://zhihaojia.medium.com/compiling-llms-into-a-megakernel-a-path-to-low-latency-inference-cf7840913c17) | whole model fused into one kernel | per-token decode 14.5 ms to 12.5 ms on A100 against a 10 ms bandwidth bound, 1.2x to 6.7x end to end |
| [Event Tensor](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2604.13327) | compiled megakernel, Qwen3-30B-A3B | 1.48x over vLLM, 1.20x over SGLang at batch 1 |
| [FlashMLA](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/FlashMLA) | MLA and DSA attention, DeepSeek models | ~3000 GB/s on H800/B200, 640 TFLOPS prefill and 410 TFLOPS decode for sparse attention |
| [DeepGEMM](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM) | a few FP8 GEMM and MoE shapes | 1550 TFLOPS on H800 |
| [KOG single-kernel engine](https://blog.kog.ai/building-a-single-kernel-latency-optimized-llm-inference-engine-on-amd-mi300x-gpus/) | batch-1 decode on MI300X | abandons matrix cores for scalar and vector ALU dot products |

Four things in that table are worth separating.

The bandwidth claim is the one that matters here. The Llama-1B megakernel work
reports that vLLM and SGLang use at most half of H100 bandwidth at low latency.
Decode on a spark is bandwidth-bound, so that headroom is the entire argument
for building.

Kernels are not the whole gap. With the same FlashInfer kernels, one
[H100 comparison](https://aimultiple.com/inference-engines) puts SGLang at
16,215 tok/s against vLLM at 12,553, a 29% spread attributed to engine
orchestration rather than math. Specialization has to reach the scheduler and
the launch path, not just the GEMMs.

Model-specific beats general even for the same operation. FlashMLA exists
because FlashAttention and xFormers optimize standard multi-head attention and
do not exploit latent compression. DeepGEMM is described by its own authors as
not a general BLAS: a few well-chosen shapes hand-tuned on CuTe and CUTLASS.
Both are the pattern this project proposes, from teams that ship at scale.

Specialization changes instruction selection, not only tiling. On MI300X at
batch 1, every matmul is a vector-matrix product, and feeding matrix-core tiles
costs more than the arithmetic they perform, so that engine uses scalar and
vector dot products instead. A general engine cannot make that choice because it
must also serve batch 64.

**Verdict.** Accepted. Published gains from specializing to one model and one
GPU run from 1.2x to 6.7x, and the reported bandwidth headroom in general
engines at low latency is roughly 2x.

None of these ran on GB10, and none used a 288-expert hybrid-attention fuel. The
numbers justify building, not any specific target for us.

**Reopen if.**

- a general engine publishes decode within 10% of the bandwidth bound on a
  sparse MoE, which would remove the headroom this rests on
